validity.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE: confirmed via two federal-docket documents. (1) The 2016 MARAD/USCG Final EIS for Port Delfin (https://www.energy.gov/sites/default/files/2018/11/f57/final-eis-0531-port-delfin-lng-main-volume-2016-11.pdf) states: 'one 700-ft, 42-inch-diameter bypass around existing West Cameron block 167 (WC 167) offshore manifold platform' interconnecting the former UTOS and HIOS pipelines; its own summary table gives Length 700 feet/213 meters and Diameter 42 inches/107 cm for this exact bypass. (2) Delfin's own March 1, 2024 DOE/FECM extension-request filing (https://www.energy.gov/sites/default/files/2024-03/Delfin%20DOE%20Extension%20request%20(030124%20FINAL).pdf, Docket Nos. 13-129-LNG/13-147-LNG) independently describes 'a new offshore pipeline to interconnect UTOS and HIOS, bypassing the platform where they currently connect,' citing the MARAD Record of Decision. Both documents ultimately trace to the same MARAD/NEPA review of Delfin's own project design (the 2024 filing cites the same ROD, and states no independent dimensions), so I treat Length/Diameter as ONE well-documented origin restated across two dockets, not two independent measurements -- see tier=medium on those fills. The July 29, 2015 Federal Register deepwater-port-license-application notice (2015-18594) and a contemporaneous May 11, 2015 oedigital.com article independently corroborate the original proposal and existence of the project this pipeline belongs to.
CLASSIFICATION: correctly classified transmission -- an interconnection bypass between two historically FERC-jurisdictional interstate transmission systems (UTOS, HIOS), not a gathering/feeder line. Fuel=Gas confirmed by the EIS.
DUPLICATE: not a duplicate of any of the other 43 roster rows. It is the unique 700-ft/0.21 km, 42-in WC167 bypass; distinct from the four ~30-in, ~6,400-ft laterals running from HIOS to each FLNGV and from the ~0.25-mile onshore supply-header pipeline described in the same EIS -- neither of those is a separate row in this batch, so no merge/relabel action is needed.
ROUTE (per orchestrator guidance to check the route against the project's own description): the routes-repo geojson (../GOIT-GGIT-pipeline-routes/data/individual-routes/gas-pipelines/P0173.geojson) is a 6-point MultiLineString, length property 0.501 km, running approximately (-93.4445, 29.4011) to (-93.4430, 29.3970) -- offshore Cameron Parish, LA. This is consistent with the EIS's WC167 bypass location (offshore, Fixed Seafloor Depth 46 ft/14 m, in the UTOS/HIOS corridor). The sheet's StartState/Province and EndState/Province = 'Gulf of Mexico' are CORRECT as recorded (a federal OCS location) -- the route's LA-coast digitized position is the offshore-snapping artifact the orchestrator flagged, not a real state-attribution error, so no Location cell edit is proposed. Minor caveat noted only: the digitized route length (0.501 km) is about 2.4x the EIS-stated physical pipe length (700 ft/0.213 km) -- most likely a simplified schematic trace of a very short offshore jumper rather than a wrong-corridor error; not material enough to recommend a route-candidate replacement.
OWNERSHIP WATCH (not staged as an attribution concern, informational only): Delfin's June 3, 2026 FID press release states that Global Infrastructure Partners, Mitsui O.S.K. Lines, Vitol and Diameter Capital Partners 'have agreed to invest in the first phase of this critical energy infrastructure project' concurrent with FID. No source states specific equity percentages in Delfin LNG LLC itself (the recorded 100% Owner1 and FERC/MARAD permit holder), so Owner1 is left as recorded; a future sweep should check for a formal ownership-percentage filing.
Overall: real, correctly classified, not a duplicate, route plausible for its stated corridor. Two clear sourcing/scope defects (Capacity, SegmentCost) and one status supersession (FID/construction/StartYear) are filed as separate concern records below.

validity.recommendation: Blank or re-derive Capacity -- 657.50 MMcf/d is not stated by any source and looks like a unit/scope transcription of the project's annual Bscf/yr export-equivalent figure, not a segment daily throughput.
validity.researcher_notes: The recorded Capacity=657.50 MMcf/d is not stated by any source found, including the current [ref] itself: oilandgaswatch.org/pipeline/4606 is a client-side-rendered SPA that returns only an empty shell to curl and to url_verifier (200, but neither '657.5' nor '657.50' is present in the fetched HTML; retried with a browser UA and probed likely API endpoints, all empty/unreachable). The number 657.5 IS in the project's own governing document but with a DIFFERENT unit and DIFFERENT scope: the 2016 Final EIS states the FLNGVs would together export LNG 'equivalent to 657.5 billion standard cubic feet per year (Bscf/yr)' -- 13.3 MMtpa for the ENTIRE 4-vessel project's annual export volume, not a daily MMcf/d throughput figure for this 700-ft segment. Recording '657.50 MMcf/d' looks like a straight transcription of that number with the wrong unit and the wrong scope (project-annual mistaken for segment-daily). A more defensible SEGMENT-relevant figure is inferable but not explicitly stated anywhere: the EIS gives each FLNGV a 'Designed Gas Flow' of 500 MMscf/d, and since gas to all 4 vessels transits the UTOS/HIOS grid this bypass enables, up to roughly 2,000 MMscf/d could pass through this interconnection -- but this is my own sum of per-vessel design-flow figures, not a number any source states for the segment itself, so I have not staged it as a sourced replacement value. Searched: both EIS volumes, the 2024 DOE extension filing, oedigital, lngprime, oilandgaswatch -- none state a segment-specific MMcf/d capacity for the WC167 bypass.

No source found states a capital/construction cost specific to the 700-ft WC167 bypass; the closest project-level cost figures found are unrelated to each other and to a segment cost (a roughly $2.5B Delfin port-facility cost estimate mentioned in a 2024 LNG Prime article, and the $5B first-FLNG-vessel FID investment announced June 2026) -- I have not proposed either as a replacement SegmentCost since neither is scoped to this segment.
